title: Start Here: C# and Python Side by Side
oneLiner: What each language is for, how your code actually runs, static versus dynamic typing, braces versus indentation, and how to use this section.
keyTakeaway: C# is compiled before it runs (to IL, then to machine code by the JIT), checks types before anything runs, and marks blocks with braces. Python is turned into bytecode and interpreted as it runs, checks types only when each line runs, and marks blocks with indentation. The ideas underneath (variables, decisions, loops, functions, collections) are the same, so learning both side by side means learning each idea once.
explanation:
This section teaches programming from the ground up in two languages at once: C# (said "C sharp") and Python. A programming language is a precise way to write instructions for a computer. You write the instructions as text, called source code, and another program turns that text into something the computer can carry out. It suits anyone from "I've edited a PLC program but never written real code" to "I code daily and want to sharpen up for interviews": skim what you know and use the predict-the-output questions to find the gaps.

How C# runs: a compiler, a program that translates a whole program before it runs, checks your code for mistakes and translates it into IL (intermediate language), a compact instruction list that isn't tied to any particular processor. When the program starts, the .NET runtime (the software that supports a running C# program) uses its JIT, or just-in-time compiler, to translate each method into the processor's own machine code the first time that method is called. A method is C#'s name for a function: a named piece of code you can call.

How Python runs: there's no separate build step. When you run a file, the standard Python (called CPython) translates it into bytecode, a similar compact instruction list, and an interpreter, a program that reads instructions one at a time and carries each one out, runs that bytecode. The practical result: C# reports many mistakes before the program runs and is fast on heavy loops; Python starts instantly and is quick to write, but is often 10 to 100 times slower on tight number-crunching loops. Compiled vs Interpreted in Computer Fundamentals goes deeper.

Types: a type is the kind of value something is, such as a whole number, text, or true or false. C# is statically typed: every variable's type is fixed in the source and the compiler checks every line before the program runs. Python is dynamically typed: a variable is just a name that can point at any value, and a type mistake shows up only when that line runs.

Blocks: C# groups lines that belong together (the body of a loop, say) with curly braces and ends each statement with a semicolon. Python uses indentation, the spaces at the start of a line: a line ending in a colon starts a block, and the block is everything indented under it.
